title: rulecad assembly
description: Objects placed together: a fit check (fits between them, joints and poses) or a plate (everything printed at once).

show.description: built: the assembly is a picture of the thing built, so its references (bought parts, boards, a module) are drawn solid in previews and on the model page, as its printed parts are; they still aren't printed or downloaded

packed.description: Written by cad plates: which assembly this plate is for, its filament, its material (each plate is one plastic: the project's, or a printed beam's own) and gap, and each part's build hash, so a changed part re-packs only its plate

fasten.description: Screwed joints: each names its screw, the parts it passes through in order, and the part it ends in. The holes are read from the parts as drawn and each screw followed along one axis; a fasten holds its parts as a fit that fastens does, lines their holes up as a holes fit does, and puts its screws on the shopping list. Draw the holes with v.fixings, and name the screw with no length: the check chooses one

joins.description: How beams are joined: each names an end of one beam (a) and a place on another (b), and its kind. A join puts its operations on both beams (a tap in a's end, an access or clearance hole across b), its screws into fasten, and a spring for the frame's solve; join.geometry checks the end meets the face square and flush where b says

defaultSnippets.label: join
defaultSnippets.description: A blind join: a's end tapped, its screw's head in b's slot

guides.description: Linear motion on a beam. A rail: a miniature rail screwed down on a beam's slotted face into slot nuts at its hole pitch, its carriages each riding its own share of the rail on a sliding joint with its true travel (<id>-1, <id>-2 ..; poses <id>-a and <id>-b put them at either end), their loads held to their ratings as joint.moment. Wheels: a printed plate (<id>-carriage-1) over a beam's face on V-wheels (<id>-wheel-1 ..) in the V tracks of the faces either side, rolling on a sliding joint (<id>-1) through the stretch from..from + length; refused on a face with no V track. A slider: a printed slider (<id>-carriage-1) in or over a slot, on a sliding joint through its stretch. Rods: two smooth rods along a face in printed holders at the stretch's ends (<id>-holder-a, <id>-holder-b, saddles screwed into the slots either side), a printed carriage (<id>-carriage-1) on two linear bearings on a sliding joint; an endstop's printed mount at a side face's address and a flag on the carriage set the joint's home. A screw: a lead screw driving a rods guide's carriage from a printed motor plate (<id>-plate) at its end a, the motor (<id>-motor) a motor item whose lead screw comes from the screw's set, a coupler, the screw, its bearings in the holders and the lead nut on the carriage. A belt: a GT2 belt driving a rail guide's one carriage, from a pulley (<id>-pulley) on a motor (<id>-motor) under a printed plate (<id>-plate) past the beam's end a, round a toothed idler (<id>-idler) on a printed block (<id>-idler-block, the tensioner: two screws in slots along the beam) past the rail's end, both belt ends in a printed clamp (<id>-clamp) on the carriage; the belt (<id>-belt) goes on the list rounded to whole metres, its ratio and the carriage's acceleration to the motor's checks, its stretch to the error budget

id.description: Its name (default g1, g2 ..): the rail item takes it

kind.description: rail (a miniature linear rail, which needs rail), wheels (a plate on V-wheels in a V-slot's tracks), slider (a printed slider in or over a slot), rods (two rods in printed holders and a printed carriage on linear bearings) screw (a lead screw and its motor driving a rods guide, which needs guide and motor) or belt (a timing belt and its motor driving a rail guide's carriage, which needs guide and motor); every kind but screw and belt needs on and length

rail.description: The rail's rule set: rail-mgn7, rail-mgn9, rail-mgn12, rail-mgn15

carriage.description: The carriage, a variant of the rail's set: MGN12C (standard, the default) or MGN12H (long)

on.description: A rail's or a slider's slotted face (x1.top, x1.top.2); for wheels, the face the plate lies over (x1.top), its wheels in the slots either side

from.description: Where the rail or the stretch starts, mm from the beam's end a (default 0)

length.description: The rail as it is cut, mm; for wheels and a slider, the stretch of the beam it runs along, mm

nut.description: A rail or rods: the slot nuts' kind (slide-in, drop-in, roll-in, square, hammer, t-bolt), for the rail's screws, or the rods' holders, motor plate and endstop mount; between two joins that close a slot at both ends, a slide-in nut is shut in (frame.nut), so give drop-in. A screw: the lead nut's rule set (t8-nut, the default)

wheel.description: Wheels: the V-wheel's rule set, v-wheel-solid (the default) or v-wheel-mini

wheels.description: Wheels: 4 (two a side, the default) or 3 (one on an eccentric)

pitch.description: Wheels: their spacing along the beam, mm (default a wheel's diameter and 15 mm, rounded up to 5)

load.description: Wheels or a slider: the printed part's design load, N (default 50 for a plate, 20 for a slider)

mode.description: A slider: over the slot (a shoe on the face, keyed into the opening; the default) or in it (a block held under its lips)

size.description: A slider: its own length along the beam, mm (default 30)

rod.description: Rods: the rods' rule set (rod-8, the default)

bearing.description: Rods: the linear bearings' rule set (lm8uu, the default, or lm8luu)

spacing.description: Rods: their distance apart across the face, mm (default room for the bearings and a lead nut's flange between)

height.description: Rods: the rods' and screw's height over the face, mm (default the least that clears the carriage, the nut, the screw's bearing, the coupler and the motor). A belt: the belt's middle over the face, mm (default the least that both the clamp's floor over the carriage and the idler's block, its M5 insert under the idler, take; give more for room under the return run for what is screwed to the carriage)

endstop.description: Rods: an endstop on a printed mount; its lever meets a flag on the carriage, and the joint homes there

at.description: An address on a face beside the rods: x1.front@80

switch.description: The switch's rule set (endstop-10t85, the default)

guide.description: A screw: the id of the rods guide whose carriage it drives; a belt: the id of the rail guide whose one carriage it drives

pulley.description: A belt: the pulley's rule set on the motor's shaft (pulley-gt2-20, the default, or pulley-gt2-16)

idler.description: A belt: the idler's rule set (idler-gt2-toothed-20, the default)

belt.description: A belt: the belt's rule set (gt2-belt-6, the default)

tension.description: A belt: each span's tension, N (default 25, an estimate)

accel.description: A belt: the carriage's acceleration it is checked at, mm/s² (default the task's accel, else 1000)

cut.description: A belt: its length as cut, mm (default the whole teeth that set its tension with the idler's block in the middle of its slots)

across.description: A belt: the idler's axle off the line that squares the belt to the travel, mm (default 0)

idlerAt.description: A belt: where the idler's block starts, mm from the beam's end a (default it ends at end b)

screw.description: A screw: the lead screw's rule set (t8-screw, the default)

support.description: A screw: the ball bearing each holder takes the screw in (bearing-608, the default), or null for none

coupler.description: A screw: the coupler from the motor's shaft to the screw (coupler-5-8, the default)

motor.description: A screw or a belt: the motor item's spec ({ "model": "28byj48", "microsteps": 1 }): its drives and leadscrew come from the guide

friction.description: A screw: the nut's friction on the screw (default the screw's set's, an estimate)

defaultSnippets.label: rail
defaultSnippets.description: An MGN12 rail on a beam's top face

defaultSnippets.label: wheels
defaultSnippets.description: A plate on four V-wheels over a V-slot beam's top face

defaultSnippets.label: a rail and a belt
defaultSnippets.description: An MGN12H rail on a 2020's top face, its carriage driven by a NEMA 17 through a GT2 belt

defaultSnippets.label: rods and a screw
defaultSnippets.description: Two 8 mm rods on a beam's top face, a carriage on LM8UUs, driven by a 28BYJ-48 through a T8 screw

task.description: What the machine is for: the tool, where it works, how fast and how accurately

deflection.description: mm of link deflection at the tool, an estimate; else worked out from the parts when there is a payload

grip.description: A compliant gripper on a servo: { servo, horn, leaf: { length, thickness, width }, travel, friction, lever, margin }

pen.description: Servo angles for the pen: { up, down }

gait.description: Poses in time: the feet by anchor, a pattern, and the body

wires.description: Wires between anchors, their length measured through every pose

anyOf.description: A run along a beam's slot: the wire follows the slot from one distance to another, held by printed cable clips at a pitch

from.description: mm from the beam's end a

cable.description: The bundle the clips hold, mm (default 6)

via.description: Anchors, path joints or runs along a slot that the wire is routed by

current.description: A: else a motor's rated current at either end, or a signal's

gravity.description: Which way down is, for masses in loads (default [0, 0, -1])

frame.description: The frame: what it is (a generator, kind with inside or outside, which expands into beams, joins and their ends before anything is built, as cad frame --expand writes out), and how its beams and joins are solved for frame.deflection, frame.stress, frame.buckling, frame.rack and frame.frequency, which beams could be printed (beam.printable), and how it is cut and heated for frame.square and frame.heat. Left out, it stands on its feet: the beam ends that carry a foot, a levelling foot, a castor plate or a stacking foot, or else the lowest beam ends, each held from moving (pinned)

kind.description: A frame generated from a size: box (four posts and a ring of beams at the bottom and top), portal (two legs and a beam across: inside and outside are [width, height]; it lies in one plane and tips over on its feet alone, so it is refused until supports says its feet are held down, as z1.a and z2.a fixed), table (four legs and a ring at the top), gantry (a box without its top beams across, and a beam riding along the two top side beams on a sliding joint) or shelf (a box with rings between, shelves of them). Its beams are z1 .. (upright), x1 .. and y1 .. (along x and y, by ring from the bottom), g (a gantry's moving beam); its corner arrangement follows the join

inside.description: The clear volume the frame encloses, [width (x), depth (y), height (z)] in mm (a portal: [width, height]); the beams go round it. Give inside or outside

outside.description: The volume the whole frame must fit in, [width, depth, height] in mm (a portal: [width, height]); the beams go within it

profile.description: Every beam's profile, a square one (2020-misumi-hfs5, 3030-generic, 4040-item-8)

join.description: How the beams meet at each corner: a kind (blind, end-tap, bracket, gusset, hidden, anchor: the upright beams run through and the others butt against their faces, each shorter by the profile's width at each end; cube: every beam butts into a corner node, each as long as the inside), or { kind, fitting, screw } as a join takes them

feet.description: What stands under the upright beams' lower ends: foot, levelling, castor or stacking (printed), or a bought foot's set by name (fitting-motedis-foot-m6-d19); left out, an end cap

caps.description: The ends no join covers: printed end caps (true, the default), a bought end cap's set by name, or false for none (join.end then names them)

braces.description: The upright sides whose corners are stiffened against racking: each join in that side becomes a bracket join with a printed corner bracket in the corner, on drop-in nuts

panels.description: Panels closing the upright sides, each cut to its bay with its clips (a box, a shelf, a gantry's two sides)

sheet.description: The sheet's material: acrylic, polycarbonate, aluminium, plywood, mdf

sides.description: Which sides (default every side that has a bay)

shelves.description: A shelf: how many rings stand between the bottom and the top, spacing its height into equal clear bays (default 1)

supports.description: Where the frame is held, by beam end ("z1.a") or a place on a beam ("x1.bottom@50%"): pinned holds it from moving and lets it turn, fixed holds it from turning too, resting holds it from moving and from twisting about the beam's own length (a beam lying across a round bar, as the beam coupon does; for a beam along x, y or z). Given, these are the only supports

limit.description: The sag allowed in every frame.deflection finding, in mm: at each load's point, each named point and along each guide whose rail gives no parallelism of its own (default: the task's accuracy, else the span of the beam it is on over 360)

points.description: Places on beams to report the sag at, beside each load's point and every guide ("x1.top@50%")

cut.description: How the beams are cut in this workshop, where it differs from the profile's set and the kit's defaults: frame.square, frame.cut and the cut list read it

tolerance.description: How far a cut length may be from the length asked, either way, in mm (default: the profile's cut_tolerance, else 0.5)

heat.description: frame.heat: the temperatures the frame works at. The beams grow with the air in the enclosure; each printed fitting is held to its plastic's softening point

air.description: The air round the frame when it runs, in degrees C (inside its enclosure)

built.description: The air it was built and squared in, in degrees C (default 20)

heaters.description: Hot things near the frame: what is within reach of one is taken at its temperature

at.description: Its middle, in the assembly's frame, mm

reach.description: How far from its middle a part is taken at that temperature, mm

printed.description: beam.printable: each beam tried printed in this plastic (the kit's printable profile of its size, lying down or standing up), the frame solved again and held to its own limits: its sags, stress, buckling, creep and lowest mode; the beams that can be printed are listed, and printed together solved once more. A plastic's set by name ("petg"), or how it prints

walls.description: Walls round every outline, in lines (3)

infill.description: The share of the inside the infill fills (0.4)

pose.description: Only this way up (both are tried where left out)

size.description: frame.size: each group of beams that must match given the lightest profile from a list that meets the frame's own limits (the sag at each load, point and guide, each beam's stress and buckling with frame.margin to spare, and the lowest mode against the task's moves), solved in every pose; a table of each group's profile, the limit that set it and its margin, and cad frame --size --write writes the profiles in

profiles.description: The profiles to choose from, by set (default MISUMI's HFS5, HFS6 and HFS8 series from 2020 to 4080). One that is not square is tried lying as drawn and turned a quarter. Choose one family whose joins fit each other: the join checks of the written frame say where they do not

groups.description: Beams that must take one profile, by group name ("rails": ["x1", "x2"]); the rest are grouped by themselves: one profile, one direction, lengths within 0.5 mm

limits.description: Limits in place of the frame checks' own

deflection.description: The sag allowed at every load, named point and guide, mm

stress.description: How many times under its alloy's strength each beam stays (default frame.margin, 2)

buckling.description: How many times its load the frame, and each grouped beam by Euler's load, must carry before it buckles (default frame.margin, 2)

frequency.description: The lowest mode's floor, Hz (default twice what the task's moves shake it at; none without a task)

by.description: What is made least (mass: no profile set in the kit gives a price per metre yet)

rack.description: frame.rack: the side push at the frame's top and the sway allowed

load.description: The side push in N, shared among the top corners (default 20, an estimate)

limit.description: The sway allowed at the top, in mm (default: the task's accuracy, else the height over 400)

loads.description: What the assembly has to do: a torque (N m) or force (N) on a joint, or a mass (kg) carried at an anchor

poses.description: Named sets of joint values ({ "hinge": 90 }), and of items' variables ("action.travel": 25: a flexure drawn bent in that pose, printed as drawn)

printInPlace.description: Items printed together as one object printed in place ("printInPlace": true on it): they come off the bed together, so the assembly order never takes them apart from each other

motor.description: A motor from @rulecad/motors: bought, not printed; its shaft turns the joint it drives

set.description: Figures that differ from the catalogue's, by name

speed.description: The motor's speed, rpm (default: what it does comfortably)

margin.description: How many times over the torque must be (default 2)

duty.description: The share of the time it runs, 0 to 1 (default 1), for its heat

screw.description: The screws that hold the motor, by a fixing's name: a thread through its plain holes, if not the size they take (M3), or a whole screw with its length and head (M3x8 hex), whose head sets the tool the order names

driver.description: The bought driver item this motor plugs into

stiffness.description: N per mm of strain, per mm of belt width

current.description: A per coil, as set on the driver (default its rated current)

cooled.description: The driver has a heat sink and moving air

microsteps.description: Steps to a full step (default 16): resolution, not accuracy

bought.description: A part from a rule set ("608", "drv8825", "fitting-motedis-end-cap-20-b6"): bought, not printed; drawn faint from its figures, with anchors from what it is. A frame's bought fitting (an end cap, a levelling foot, a hinge) placed at a beam's address is checked against that beam's profile, and its price goes on cad list

fitting.description: A printed fitting from @rulecad/frames, drawn from a profile's and its slot nuts' rules and sized from a named load (a join with "fitting": "printed" adds one for itself; a panel adds its clips, a door its hinges, handle and catch). A bracket, gusset or splice is sized by finite elements; the others by beam formulas, each reporting its grams and margin. In its fitted frame: a bracket's x along b's face away from a, y up a, z across; a plate's x along b, y along a, its contact face at z = 0

kind.description: A nut-carrier is a printed block that slides in a slot holding a hex nut or a heat-set insert (face, thread, holds, length, count, pitch, load)

profile.description: The profile the base leg or the plate lies on

other.description: A bracket's: the profile its upright leg lies on, where not the same

face.description: The face of the profile it lies on (top, top.2): its slot sizes the tongue and the nut

brace.description: A bracket's brace across its inside corner

load.description: The design load in N, across beam a at the fitting's screw (default 100)

count.description: A plate's screws on each arm (default 2)

part.description: A hinge's leaf (frame, door) or a levelling foot's part (body, pad): an item each

sheet.description: The panel's or door's thickness, in mm

standoff.description: A latch's or catch's: the door's inner face over the beam's face (a hinge's standoff)

holds.description: A nut-carrier's: a hex nut slid in from the side (the default) or a heat-set insert pressed in from below

device.description: A device mount's: the rule set its holes are read from (supply-24v, cnc-shield-v3)

variant.description: A device mount's: the device's variant

turn.description: A device mount's: the device's x from the slot's line, degrees

offset.description: A device mount's: the device's middle across the slot, mm

size.description: A fan mount's fan, mm: 40, 60, 80, 92 or 120

rod.description: A rod holder's or carriage's: the rods' rule set

bearing.description: A carriage's linear bearings' rule set

leadNut.description: A rod holder's or carriage's: the lead nut's rule set

support.description: A rod holder's: the screw's ball bearing's rule set

flag.description: A carriage's endstop flag: where its tip reaches, { y, z }

motor.description: A motor plate's: the motor's rule set (28byj48, nema14, nema17)

coupler.description: A motor plate's: the coupler's { length, D }

switch.description: An endstop mount's: the switch's rule set

pulley.description: A belt plate's: the pulley's rule set

idler.description: A belt idler block's: the idler's rule set

belt.description: A belt part's: the belt's rule set

across.description: A belt plate's or idler block's: the pulley's or idler's middle off the slot's line, mm

least.description: A belt plate's: the least height of the belt's middle over the face, mm

lift.description: A belt plate's: how much further up its shaft the pulley stands, mm (default 0), to raise the belt without a thicker plate

tension.description: A belt part's: each span's tension, N

rise.description: A belt clamp's or idler block's: the belt's middle over the carriage's top, or over the face

stretch.description: A belt idler block's: the belt's stretch at its tension, mm

carriageHoles.description: A belt clamp's: the carriage's tapped holes, [[x, y], ...] from its top's middle

toward.description: An endstop mount's: which way across the face its lever reaches

pose.description: fit (the default): in its place, as the item's at and rotate put it; print: laid as it prints, for a plate (cad plates writes it so)

panel.description: A panel from @rulecad/frames: a sheet cut to the bay of four beams it closes, on their faces that look along out, held by printed clips at a pitch; with door, a door on printed hinges that turns on a joint

bay.description: The four beam items round it, in order

out.description: The way its face looks, square to the bay

hinge.description: The beam of the bay its hinges go on

mount.description: A bought board's or supply's printed mount on a beam (@rulecad/frames' deviceMountModel), its holes read from the item's rule set: the mount goes at a slotted face's address, the item on it, and the screws into the slot and into the device are fastens

on.description: An address on a beam's slotted face: rail.top@200

turn.description: The device's x from the beam's line, degrees

offset.description: The device's middle across the slot, mm

load.description: N on the device at its farthest hole (default 50)

screw.description: A board's screws, where not the largest its holes pass

beam.description: A length of a profile from @rulecad/frames: bought and cut to length, faint in previews, or printed; placed by its ends (from, to, roll) or by at and rotate

profile.description: A profile's name: 2020-misumi-hfs5, profile-4040-item-8, or a set in this workspace's rules/

length.description: mm from end a to end b; may be left out when from and to are both given

printed.description: A printed beam (@rulecad/frames printed beams): true, or how it prints. A printed beam is a printed part, weighed by the plastic laid, on a plate, off the cut list; a bought one is false, the default

pose.description: lying (the default): on its bottom face, its layers along it; standing: on end a, its section the layer

walls.description: Walls round every outline, in lines (3)

infill.description: The share of the inside the infill fills (0.4)

end.description: What a tapped end becomes in print: a heat-set insert (the default) or a captive nut

pull.description: A slot nut's design pull in N (100)

laid.description: A printed beam drawn as it prints, for a plate (cad plates writes it so)

material.description: A material set in place of the profile's alloy: al6063-t5, or a plastic

ops.description: Operations on the beam, each a line on its sheet and a cut in its solid, placed by an address on the beam and dimensioned from end a

to.description: A beam's end b, with from its end a

roll.description: Degrees a beam placed by its ends turns about its own axis, a toward b; at 0 its top faces up (+z), or +y when it stands upright

have.description: A bought part or a motor already in hand: cad list, the kit's buy.csv and its build page list it as in hand, apart from what is to buy. Only on a bought or motor item

from.description: For a beam: its end a, [x, y, z]. For an object: inputs worked out from items built before it, { input: expression }

engage.description: a goes at least this far (mm) onto b along the joint between them: a part slid onto a shaft or a pin, not resting on its end

radius.description: With engage: how near the joint's axis to look (mm, default 10)

shaft.description: a or b is a motor, and the other takes its shaft: reads the bore from the part as drawn; slide: the bore as printed (the drawn gap less half the printer's hole_comp) must clear the shaft, as a part printed in place needs

seat.description: a or b is a bought bearing, and the other its printed seat: reads the pocket as drawn against the bearing's rules and the printer's fit (fit.seat)

fastens.description: a and b are fastened together (pins, a press, a clip): what holds a part that has no joint. Where screws hold them, use a fasten instead: it knows the screw, checks its holes and lists it

fastener.description: What does the fastening: in words (two push pins), named on the shopping list and the assembly step as written; or pins, { "pin": "snap pin 4x6", "count": 2 }, found in the parts' holes and checked (fit.pin): each hole against the one @rulecad/fixings draws for the pin and the printer, the pin's length against the parts, and the load; or magnets, { "magnet": "disc magnet 8x3", "count": 2 }, found in the parts' pockets and checked (fit.magnet): each pocket against the one @rulecad/fixings draws for the magnet and the printer, its depth and floor, and their pull against the load. A screw is a fasten's, which chooses its length and counts it

access.description: <item>.<anchor>: where the screw's tool comes from, its z axis pointing out along the screw. Whatever stands on that line goes on after the screw; if nothing can, assembly.order says so

holes.description: A holes fit: a circuit board's part (pcb.board) whose mounting holes are followed down into the part named by into. Where the board is screwed there, a fasten with "holes" says it and knows the screw: cad check suggests it, cad add fasten --from-fits writes it

depth.description: With holes: how far each screw's path must be clear (mm)

direction.description: With holes: up for screws from below

ring.description: With holes: how far round each screw there must be material (mm, default the hole's diameter)

into.description: With holes: the part the screws go into

within.description: With an anchor name (item@anchor): only faces this close to it (mm, default 10)

pins.description: Pins that hold a fit's two parts together: found in round holes of part a that go on into part b

pin.description: A pin by name, as @rulecad/fixings reads it: snap pin 4x6 (a printed snap pin, 4 mm peg, 6 mm shaft; barb 0.6 after it for another barb), dowel 3x12 (a steel ISO 8734 dowel; ISO 2338 after it for an unhardened one), filament pin 1.75x12, printed pin 4x10

count.description: How many (default 1): that many holes must be found

fit.description: A plain pin's fit in its holes: press (it grips) or slip (it turns). Left out, each hole may be either

load.description: N across the joint, shared by the pins: each pin's shear and its hole's bearing are held to it with about twice the margin

pull.description: N along the pins, shared by them: what snap pins must hold before they let go

magnets.description: Magnets that hold a fit's two parts together: found in round pockets of part a or part b

magnet.description: A magnet by name, as @rulecad/fixings reads it: disc magnet 8x3 (8 mm across, 3 mm thick, N35 unless a grade follows: disc magnet 8x3 N52), block magnet 10x5x2

count.description: How many (default 1): that many pockets must be found

fit.description: How each sits in its pocket: pressed, glued, or held by crush ribs. Left out, each pocket may be any of them

load.description: N pulling the parts apart, shared by the magnets: their pull is held to it with about twice the margin

gap.description: mm between each magnet and what it pulls on, when the parts are together (paint, a skin, air): its pull falls across it

beamAddress.description: An address on a beam, without its item: an end (a, b), an end's bore (a.1), or a face's place with a distance from end a (top@120), from end b (top@-20) or a share of the length (top@50%), the second place of a face top.2@120

beamOp.description: An operation on a beam (@rulecad/frames OPS): each takes only its own keys, and is refused by name otherwise

op.description: cut: square to length; mitre: an end at an angle about a named face; tap: a thread in an end bore; access: a hole across, in line with a slot, for a key; drill: through one wall or right through, plain or tapped; counterbore: a seat for a head; pocket: milled by outline; notch: a slot's lips cut away; deburr: named so the sheet asks for it

thread.description: A thread by name (M5): sizes the hole, the tap or the seat through @rulecad/fixings

head.description: A counterbore's head: cap, button, hex or pan; an access hole's, the head its hex key turns: cap (the default), button or countersunk

diameter.description: mm, in place of a thread's figure

depth.description: mm from the face or the end

through.description: A drilled hole through one wall (the default) or right through the beam

angle.description: A mitre's angle from square, degrees

about.description: The face a mitre's angle is seen on

long.description: The side a mitred beam's length is measured on

outline.description: A pocket's outline, points [along, across] about the address

length.description: A notch's length along the beam, mm

address.description: An anchor by name, <item>.<anchor>; on a beam an end (x1.a, x1.b), an end bore (x1.a.1), or a face with a distance from end a (x1.top@120), from end b (x1.top@-20) or a share of the length (x1.top@50%), the second slot of a face x1.top.2@120

join.description: Two beams joined: an end of one (a), a place on the other (b), and how (kind)

kind.description: blind: a's end tapped, a button-head screw's head in b's slot, an access hole across b. end-tap: a's end tapped, a cap screw through a hole drilled across b. bracket, gusset and splice with "fitting": "printed" add a printed fitting and its screws; bracket, gusset, splice, hidden and anchor with a bought fitting's set by name add that fitting, its screws and the holes it needs. The rest (cube, mitre's key, pivot, printed) are checked where they meet and stiffen the frame by an estimate; their fittings come in later releases

a.description: A beam's end: y1.a, or one bore of it where the end has several (y1.a.2)

b.description: A place on the other beam where a's end (its bore's axis) meets it: a face with a distance from its end a (x1.back@120, x1.top@-20, x1.top@50%), or an end (x1.b) for a splice, mitre or corner

fitting.description: For a kind with a fitting: printed, or a bought fitting's rule set by name (fitting-motedis-bracket-20-b6), or bought to be told which sets there are. Printed, a bracket, gusset or splice join adds the fitting as an item, placed from where the beams are, its screws into slot nuts in both beams as fastens, and its own stiffness by finite elements. A bought set on a bracket, gusset, splice, hidden or anchor join adds its item (a reference, listed with its price), its screws into the set's nuts as fastens, the hole a beam needs for it, and its set's stiffness, an estimate until the joint rig measures it

brace.description: A printed bracket's brace across its inside corner

face.description: A printed gusset's: the face of b it lies on (front, back.2), one of the two square to a; left out, the one its frame from the beams' directions gives. A generated frame names the face looking out of the frame

shape.description: A printed gusset's shape: L (one arm along each beam) or T (a bar along b on both sides of a, where b has room). Left out, a T where b has room for its bar, else an L. A generated gantry gives L at its top side beams, where a T's bar would rise beside the post into the moving beam's path

load.description: A printed fitting's design load in N, across beam a at its screw (default 100): it is sized to about twice the margin at it

nut.description: A printed fitting's slot nuts' kind (default: the strongest made for the slot)

screw.description: For blind and end-tap: the screw by thread and head (M5 button), where not the end bore's thread with the kind's head

fasten.description: A screwed joint: the screw by thread and head, the parts it passes in order, the part it ends in, and where the screws go (at, an anchor each, or holes, a part's own holes)

defaultSnippets.label: screws in a part's own holes

screw.description: The screw, by its thread and head: M3 cap, M4 button, M3x12 countersunk, 6-32 UNC cap (the names @rulecad/fixings reads). With no length in the name, the shortest sold length that fits is chosen

through.description: The parts the screw passes through, in order from under its head: items (bracket) or item.part (bracket.body). Each needs a clearance hole for the thread

into.description: The part the screw ends in: a pilot, a tapped or printed thread, an insert's hole or a nut's seat there, or a clearance hole with nut. Or a slot on a beam (x1.top, x1.top.2, x1.top@120): the screw ends in a slot nut under the slot's lips, the one made for that slot and thread (nut chooses its kind), and each screw lies over a slot's centre line (fasten.slot)

at.description: One screw at each anchor: a point on its axis (bracket.h1), the anchor's axis along the screw

holes.description: In place of at: a part whose holes are the screws' places, found in the part as drawn (a circuit board: its mounting holes)

nut.description: What holds the screw where the part it ends in does not: true or hex, square, lock. It sits on that part's far face, or in a nut's seat drawn there. Into a beam's slot, the slot nut's kind: slide-in, drop-in, roll-in, hammer, square or t-bolt (left out, the strongest made for the slot). A slide-in or square nut enters only from an open end of the slot (frame.nut, frame.preload)

washer.description: A plain washer under the head

length.description: The screw's length in mm, where the name gives none: checked for reaching, bottoming out and standing proud

torque.description: The tightening torque, N m: the pressure under the head is then held against the material it sits on (fasten.seat)

support.description: What takes this joint's tipping load: bought bearings, or printed clips (read by FE)

pitch.description: Diameter the clips stand on, mm

cell.description: FE cell for the clips, mm (0.8 by default)

linkCell.description: FE cell for the link bent beyond this joint (link.deflection), mm (by default a third of the link's thinnest side, 1 to 4)

errors.description: What this joint adds to the error at the tool, degrees, by name (play, twist, bearing): an expression reading a rule, so a measurement moves it

brake.description: What holds this joint with the power off (a ratchet, a detent): counted by motor.holds

mesh.description: Gears: this joint's gear meshes with the gear on the joint named by with, which drives it

planetary.description: A planetary gearbox: one of sun, carrier and ring held, the one named by drive turning, the rest following it in phase

output.description: A compound planetary: a second ring, on the planets' second step
